title: A membrane-voltage change can induce eyes almost anywhere in the Xenopus body

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A membrane-voltage change can induce eyes almost anywhere in the Xenopus body

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In Xenopus laevis, misexpressing potassium channels to change membrane voltage induces ectopic eyes in many posterior regions including the gut, showing that cells outside the anterior neural field are competent to build eyes when given a higher-level bioelectric signal, contrary to conclusions drawn from prompting cells with the 'master eye gene' Pax6.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Bioelectricity as the Interface to Multicellularity › Applications: Modulating Endogenous Bioelectric Cues

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: It was always thought that cells outside the anterior neural field in vertebrates were not competent to build eyes. But prior studies prompted cells with the so‐called master eye gene Pax6 [123]. It turns out that a higher‐level signal (V mem change) can induce eyes almost anywhere in the body.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Bioelectricity as the Interface to Multicellularity › Applications: Modulating Endogenous Bioelectric Cues”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos injected with potassium channel mRNA (author's lab's prior work, ref [120])

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Eye identity and location are directly scoreable, and the original published experiment can resolve sampled Xenopus regions. Lack of known complete raw data and the broad wording prevent treating the claim as fully resolvable now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map ectopic eye incidence, location and tissue composition after potassium-channel misexpression and compare posterior competence with matched Pax6 perturbations. Histologically complete eyes across many posterior tissues support the claim; confinement to anterior fields or non-eye pigmented spots refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Almost anywhere is broader than sampled body regions.

Raw embryo-level images and injection maps may not be public.

Channel expression can have indirect developmental effects.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.85
analysis feasibility: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.95
data existence: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Eye location after a specified channel misexpression is a standard, countable outcome, and the original paper reports percentages and body positions. Those embryo scores are not deposited, and public gene-expression resources for Pax6 do not contain the voltage experiment needed to compare competence. An outside reanalysis cannot confirm or refute the result without the raw series or a new experiment.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Misexpress potassium channels in Xenopus blastomeres outside the anterior neural field and score eye structures by location, including gut and tail, against lineage-tracer and Pax6-only controls. Eyes in posterior tissues after a voltage change, and not after the tracer alone, would support the claim; restriction of eyes to the anterior neural field would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Embryo-level locations and histological scores are published as summaries, not as a public table.

There is no independent open replication dataset.

Pax6 expression atlases do not record the voltage perturbation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.25
data existence: 0.3
data adequacy: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.88
